A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeoBPE research. The main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation, renumbering and terminology changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original compression/reconstruction experiments, downstream prediction results, ablations, backbone generation and expert-agreement analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds predicted-structure tokenization, larger language-model experiments, robustness analyses and sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: The clustering, Geo-Pair merging, glue-angle optimization, TreeLSTM transfer encoder and autoregressive modeling procedures are retained. New Algorithms 10–11 detail learned-vocabulary tokenization of unseen structures, already described and evaluated in v1. Expanded pseudocode and parameter-selection guidance do not establish an algorithmic redesign.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds 550,000 Swiss-Prot structures predicted by AlphaFold for tokenization and language-model training, substantially extending the original experimental-structure coverage. Appendix C adds agreement evaluation against eight DSSP secondary-structure classes. The original PDB, CAMEO, CASP14 and downstream benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Appendix F.2 adds explicit designability comparisons with ProtDiff (11.8%) and FoldingDiff (14.2%). These are numerical reference comparisons; the PDFs do not establish fresh runs of those baselines. The existing tokenizer comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds downstream training-fraction controls and a 65.9M-parameter SSLM alongside the 7.3M model. Its scaling evaluation generates 50–128-residue proteins, whereas the original experiment samples an empirical length prior averaging approximately 214 residues. Appendix K also specifies fixed bond lengths for transfer and w_t=1.0 for the updated Pareto evaluation.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing ablations with downstream-data sweeps (Table 4), reconstruction after 1% tokenizer training (Table 5), secondary-structure agreement (Tables 8–9), and robustness across unusualness, length and fold types (Figure 11). Tables 16–18 and Figure 13 add systematic sensitivity tests of vocabulary resolution, binning, glue optimization and bond-length handling.

E5.justification: Appendix I newly reports per-bin means and standard deviations, distribution boxplots, and Pearson correlations with 95% confidence intervals. These describe variation across proteins and uncertainty in correlations, rather than repeated-training uncertainty. The 1,000-random-partition agreement baseline was already present in v1.

E6.justification: V2 updates the GeoBPE Pareto points and corrects Table 1's functional-site mean from 79.93 to 80.20 while retaining the individual split scores. It adds extensive analysis results, Swiss-Prot reconstruction scores, and scaled-generation results of 0.376/0.405 scTM and 12%/21% designability. The generation additions use different settings from v1's retained SSLM results.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the per-link transform's dihedral argument and corresponding glue definition from phi_{i+1} to phi_i. Appendix I defines structural unusualness as 100 times one minus the best-hit TM-score. The principal geometric derivations, tokenizer principles and complexity analysis remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about geometric BPE, compression, generalization, data efficiency, downstream transfer, generation and interpretability. The expanded evidence does not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations separating tokenizer data efficiency from downstream-model underfitting, explaining hyperparameter tradeoffs, and relating reconstruction to fold type and size. The limitations now explicitly frame SSLM as a tokenizer comparison and acknowledge noncompetitive backbone-design quality, while dropping v1's explicit pretrained-PLM-dependence and larger-codebook caveats. New scaling and secondary-structure interpretations substantially broaden the discussion.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit unseen-structure tokenization pseudocode, extensive parameter-selection instructions, loss-weight settings, measured CPU runtimes and the larger Transformer's configuration. It also specifies ProteinMPNN with eight sequences per structure and OmegaFold for scTM assessment, where v1 described generic tools. These materially improve procedural documentation without establishing that every retained experiment changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for UniProt, AlphaFold DB, ProtDiff, FoldingDiff and OmegaFold, positioning the scaling experiment relative to diffusion-based generation. The main related-work discussion and positioning against structural alphabets, VQ-VAEs and biological BPE remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The methods exposition gains organized notation and an expanded explanation of grounding, quantization, refinement and synchronization. Transfer is distinguished through the GeoBPE-TRANSFER name. The hyperparameter appendix is rebuilt into documentation, application-specific guidance and sensitivity sections, while SSLM framing and limitations are substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 adds the toy-geometry diagram, robustness plots, stopping-rule illustration, sensitivity panels and numerous analysis tables. The existing flowchart moves into Methods, and the retained expert-case figures are redesigned as explicit merge trees with arrows and span labels. The Pareto plot is redrawn and the generation table gains scaling rows.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence and guidance on practical scalability, parameter sensitivity and unseen-structure encoding. The 550,000-structure benchmark, controlled data and sensitivity studies, robustness analysis, and explicit inference algorithms provide stronger validation and reproducibility. Changed generation lengths limit the scaling conclusions, and secondary-structure score conventions remain unclear, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and procedural clarity.
